messages.content: Denver is done, so I want to start the MLK weekend idea for D.C. It would be me, Arjun, and Leela, flying from Atlanta Saturday Jan. 17 and coming back Monday Jan. 19. Maybe Friday night if school and work line up, but I'm not sure yet. Main goal is museums, so ideally DCA and a hotel near Metro and the Mall. Breakfast included would be nice, but not if it pushes us too far out.

Good timing to frame it now. A few details will drive the shortlist: whether Friday is truly possible, your rough hotel budget, whether one room with two queens works, and how much of a fare premium DCA can carry over BWI before it stops being worth it. For a short museum weekend, DCA plus a Metro-adjacent hotel near the Mall is the simplest baseline.

One room is fine, preferably two queens but a king plus sofa would work if the room is bigger. I'd like to stay roughly under $325 before tax if we can, and I'd like the hotel to be solidly rated, like 4-plus if we're using Google or similar. No rental car.

Then I would compare airports this way: DCA is best for convenience, with short Metro or rideshare access and less wasted time. BWI can be cheaper, but once you add train or rideshare time, it can take 60 to 90 minutes door to door. IAD is usually the least attractive for this specific museum weekend unless fares are much better. If Friday becomes a late-evening departure, the extra hotel night may not buy enough usable sightseeing time.
Which hotel areas should I actually look at? I don't know if Penn Quarter, Capitol Hill, or Arlington makes more sense.

Penn Quarter or Metro Center keeps you close to restaurants, Metro, and several museums, but breakfast may be paid. L'Enfant Plaza or the Wharf area is very convenient for Air and Space, Natural History, and the Mall, with easy dining nearby. Capitol Hill or Navy Yard can have roomier suite hotels with breakfast, but you will spend more time getting to the main museum cluster. Arlington or Crystal City is easy from DCA but less ideal for popping back to the hotel midday.
Air and Space and Natural History are the two definite ones. Maybe African American History if we can get timed entry. I don't want every day to start with a long Metro ride.

That points toward L'Enfant Plaza, the Wharf, or Penn Quarter first. I would keep included breakfast as a bonus rather than a requirement for this one, because the suite-style free-breakfast hotels are more likely to be farther from the museums. A reasonable shortlist would be: central Mall-area hotel with paid breakfast, or a Navy Yard/Capitol Hill suite with included breakfast and more space.
Can you help me rough out Friday versus Saturday before I ask Arjun?

Yes. Friday night only helps if you can leave early enough to be in D.C. before bedtime. Otherwise you pay for an extra hotel night and still start Saturday tired. Saturday morning keeps cost down and still gets you to D.C. late morning if you take a nonstop into DCA. For Monday, I would avoid leaving too early if you want one last museum stop.
If BWI saves around $250 total, is that worth considering?

It is worth considering, but not automatically worth choosing. For three people, a $250 fare savings may shrink after train or rideshare costs, and you would lose time on both ends. For this short trip with a child and museums as the point, I would need the BWI savings to be more like $300 to $350 total before it clearly beats DCA.
Okay. What should I ask Arjun tonight before we narrow it?

Ask him these: can Friday departure happen before about 6 p.m., or is Saturday morning more realistic; how much extra he is willing to pay for DCA over BWI; whether central location beats free hotel breakfast; whether two queens is required; how late Monday is okay before Tuesday school feels rough; and which timed-entry museum matters most. If Friday is not useful and DCA is not wildly more expensive, I would lean Saturday morning ATL-DCA, Monday afternoon return, and a central Metro hotel.

messages.content: I got the answers on D.C. No Friday early release, and Arjun can't leave work before late afternoon anyway, so let's drop Friday. Can we compare the strongest Saturday-to-Monday flight and hotel combinations?

That makes the weekend cleaner. I would focus on three combinations: A) convenience plan: Saturday morning nonstop ATL-DCA, Monday afternoon nonstop DCA-ATL, central Mall-area hotel with paid breakfast; B) lower hotel-cost plan: same DCA flights, suite hotel farther out with included breakfast; C) fare-saver plan: BWI flights plus central hotel. C only wins if the fare gap is big enough to justify the extra ground transfer.
How much extra time is BWI really adding? The fares I saw were cheaper, but not dramatically.

Plan on roughly an extra hour each way compared with DCA, sometimes more if you are juggling train timing, bags, and a child. DCA to the Mall area can be 15 to 25 minutes. BWI to the same hotel is usually closer to 70 to 90 minutes door to door unless everything lines up perfectly.
Then I think BWI is out unless the savings are huge. The hotel decision is harder. The central one is about $322 before tax with breakfast paid. The suite option is about $268 and includes breakfast.

For two nights, the central hotel is about $108 more before tax, plus probably $60 to $90 total for simple breakfasts. So call it around $170 to $210 more all-in. What it buys you is less Metro time, easier breaks if the weather is bad, and a simpler Monday morning before the return flight. The suite buys space and breakfast, but not as much convenience.
Can you name the two hotel options and the practical tradeoff?

The central option I would keep is Hilton Washington DC National Mall The Wharf, showing about a 4.3 Google rating, right by L'Enfant Plaza with very easy museum access and nearby Wharf dining. Breakfast is paid. The farther suite option is Residence Inn Washington Capitol Hill/Navy Yard, about a 4.4 Google rating, with larger rooms and included breakfast, but it adds Metro or rideshare time to the museum core.
The central one sounds better for this trip. I just hate paying for breakfast when the other one includes it.

I get that. For a longer stay, I would give the suite more weight. For two nights, the central location is likely to matter more than free breakfast, especially if Sunday is cold or rainy. You can keep breakfast cheap with coffee, pastries, or a quick hotel cafe stop, and you are not locked into a long transfer before the first museum.
What about the return flight? There is a cheaper midday one, and then the afternoon nonstop.

The midday return saves some money but basically ends the trip after breakfast. The afternoon nonstop lets you do one final museum or a relaxed lunch, then head to DCA without rushing. If the afternoon fare difference is modest, I would choose it for the short weekend.
There is also a 6:30-ish return. Too late?

For an adult-only trip it would be fine. With Leela and school the next day, I would avoid it unless the savings are substantial. A return around 4:30 to 5:00 p.m. is the better middle ground: useful daytime in D.C. without getting home too late.
Can we get adjacent seats? And if possible put me by the window.

On the DCA nonstop option, there is a standard three-seat block available on both legs right now. I would put you in A, Leela in B, and Arjun in C, so you have the window and everyone stays together. I would not pay extra just to move a few rows forward if the standard block is available.
Is basic economy too risky for that?

Yes, I would avoid basic economy for this trip. The savings are not worth losing advance seat selection with a child. Main Cabin or the equivalent fare is the right choice so you can select the three-seat block now and make changes more easily if schedules move.
What if we need to cancel because of weather or someone gets sick?

For the hotel, choose the refundable rate if it is only a small difference; it is worth it for a January family weekend. For flights, Main Cabin should give you a credit rather than a full refund unless you buy refundable, so the key is making sure the names and dates are right before ticketing.
Okay, let's go with the central hotel and the afternoon return. Use two queens if available.

Done. The plan is set as Saturday Jan. 17 ATL-DCA nonstop in the morning, Monday Jan. 19 DCA-ATL nonstop around 4:45 p.m., Main Cabin, with three adjacent seats selected on both legs and you in the window seat. Hotel is Hilton Washington DC National Mall The Wharf for Jan. 17-19, one room with two queens on the refundable rate. Breakfast is not included, so I noted nearby quick breakfast options and the hotel cafe as the workaround.

messages.content: Can you give me the final D.C. rundown? Flights and hotel are set, but I want the practical checklist: Atlanta airport timing, DCA to hotel, luggage drop if the room is not ready, food, breakfast, museums, weather, and whether any better seats opened.

For the Saturday morning ATL-DCA flight, leave Decatur around 5:45 to 6:00 a.m. for a comfortable airport buffer. If PreCheck is not on all three boarding passes, use regular family security timing. At DCA, take the Yellow Line to L'Enfant Plaza if service is normal, or a short rideshare if the weather is ugly. Drop bags at the hotel if the room is not ready, then start with lunch and the Mall.
We are not checking bags. Leela may not have PreCheck, so assume regular security. The hotel says check-in is 4.

Then pack one small day bag inside a carry-on with gloves, chargers, snacks, and anything needed before the room is ready. Check in online, ask for early availability when you arrive, and if not, leave the roller bags with the bell desk.
Sunday may be cold rain, and I still have to handle one timed-entry museum.

Book Air and Space timed entry now if that is still a priority. For rain, cluster indoor stops: Air and Space, Natural History, American History, or Portrait Gallery. Avoid planning a long Mall walk in the cold rain; use Metro or short rideshares between clusters if needed.
Breakfast and seats?

Seats are still the same three-together blocks, with you in the window on both legs; I would leave them unless a better no-fee adjacent row appears at check-in. For breakfast, since it is not included, use the hotel cafe or a nearby coffee spot and pack a backup snack for Leela. Last checks: boarding passes, IDs, hotel confirmation, museum timed entry, umbrellas, comfortable shoes, chargers, and contactless payment for Metro.
